table.note: A member-rate candidate on the self-paced route lands at $2,082 all-in including one Houston travel day. A non-member on the five-day instructor-led online route lands at $6,283. Neither figure includes the codes and standards the examination draws on, which are bought separately, or the technician's paid time away from billable work. The two avoidable lines, $200 late and $350 reschedule, are the ones sponsors actually pay, because API runs three examination windows a year and each application deadline falls two to four months ahead of its window.

facets.q: What is the realistic all-in cost to sponsor a field technician through API 510?
facets.a: $2,082 at the low end and $6,283 at the high end for the 2026 windows. The floor is API's $875 member examination fee, a $999 self-paced prep course and one travel day at the $208 Houston per diem rate. The ceiling swaps in the $1,125 non-member fee and a $4,950 five-day instructor-led course. Add the technician's paid time away and a $350 reschedule fee if the date moves.

facets.q: Is getting an API 510 still worth the time and cost in 2026?
facets.a: Yes for anyone working owner-user pressure vessel scopes. The certificate is a bid qualification on refinery and petrochemical inspection contracts, not merely a salary lever, so it changes what work a person can be assigned to. Payscale's certification data shows $131,000 average for holders against $62,807 for the generic pressure vessel inspector title. The all-in cost returns inside one turnaround season.

facets.q: Can you take the API 510 exam remotely in 2026?
facets.a: No. API withdrew remote proctoring for its core inspector programmes. The published position is that API 510, 570, 653, 1169 and 1184 are not available for remote testing; they run as computer-based examinations at Prometric test centres only. Remote proctoring through ProProctor stays available for other API examinations including 571, 577, 580 and 936. Budget a travel day and a hotel night.

facets.q: What experience do you need to sit API 510?
facets.a: One year with a bachelor's degree in engineering or technology, two years with a two-year associate degree or certificate, three years with a high school diploma, and five years with no formal education. All of it must have been acquired within the previous ten years while employed by or contracted to an authorised inspection agency, and at least one year must be supervising or performing inspection.

facets.q: How often do you recertify an API 510 and what does it cost?
facets.a: Every three years, at $745 for API members and $855 for non-members. Each three-year cycle requires 24 Continuing Professional Development hours, with a maximum of 12 hours carried into the next cycle, plus continued inspection experience of at least twenty percent of working time. A six-year open-book web quiz sits on top of the three-year cycle.

facets.q: When are the 2026 and 2027 API 510 exam windows?
facets.a: The 2026 windows run 2 to 23 January, 8 to 29 May and 4 to 25 September, with application deadlines of 31 October 2025, 13 March 2026 and 3 July 2026. The 2027 windows run 2 to 22 January, 7 to 28 May and 3 to 24 September, with deadlines of 29 October 2026, 4 March 2027 and 2 July 2027. Missing a deadline costs $200.

sections.heading: The all-in number, line by line
paragraphs: A sponsorship costs between $2,082 and $6,283 per candidate for the 2026 windows. The floor is API's member rate of $875, a $999 self-paced online prep programme and one travel day at the $208 Houston federal per diem. The ceiling is the $1,125 non-member rate, a $4,950 five-day instructor-led online course and the same travel day. Everything else that appears on the invoice is avoidable rather than inherent.

API publishes the fees directly and they are not negotiable. Initial certification is $875 for members and $1,125 for non-members. Recertification is $745 and $855. A late application costs $200 and a reschedule costs $350. Those last two are the lines that surprise sponsors, because API runs only three examination windows a year and each application deadline lands two to four months before the window it belongs to.

What the published fees exclude matters as much as what they include. The examination draws on API 510 itself plus recommended practices 571, 572, 576 and 577, and ASME Sections V, VIII Division 1 and IX, and those publications are bought separately. The candidate's paid study time is the largest uncosted line in most sponsorships and the one that decides whether the money works. Budget it explicitly rather than assuming evenings.

sections.heading: What API publishes and what it does not
paragraphs: API's Individual Certification Programs pages carry the fee schedule and the examination calendar, and both are precise. The 2026 windows are 2 to 23 January, 8 to 29 May and 4 to 25 September, with application deadlines of 31 October 2025, 13 March 2026 and 3 July 2026. The 2027 windows are 2 to 22 January, 7 to 28 May and 3 to 24 September. Plan backwards from a deadline, never forwards from a start date.

The examination structure is published too. The API 510 day runs seven and a half hours: a short tutorial, 2.75 hours of closed-book questions, a forty-five-minute lunch and 3.75 hours of open-book questions. There are 170 questions of which 140 are scored, split 110 closed-book and 60 open-book. Codes appear as searchable PDF documents on the examination computer during the open-book portion, and paper copies are not permitted in the centre.

What API does not publish is a pass rate, a prep-course endorsement or an official study-hours estimate. Any provider quoting a pass percentage is quoting its own cohort, not API's. Treat those numbers as marketing and judge a course on its question bank, its access period and whether it drills the damage mechanisms in recommended practice 571, which is where most candidates lose closed-book marks on the day.

sections.heading: The prep-course market runs $999 to $5,950
paragraphs: Published prices bracket the market cleanly. Atlas API Training sells a self-paced online API 510 course at $999 with sixty hours of content, six months of access, more than 900 practice questions and a free repeat if the candidate fails. PetroKnowledge sells a five-day instructor-led course at $4,950 online and $5,950 in person in Dubai or Barcelona. That is a six-fold spread across the same published body of knowledge.

The spread buys instructor time and an enforced schedule, not additional content. A self-motivated candidate with a study plan and a question bank passes on the $999 route. A candidate who has not sat a formal examination in fifteen years, or who works rotation and cannot protect study evenings, passes more reliably with the classroom week, and $350 of reschedule fees plus a forfeited window costs more than the difference between the two routes.

Judge courses on three things: whether the question bank exercises open-book navigation as well as closed-book recall, whether the access period spans a full examination window, and whether a failed first attempt is covered. Atlas publishes all three on its course page. Providers that publish none of them are asking for trust they have not evidenced, and a purchase order should not leave the building until they do.

sections.heading: The Prometric constraint: three windows, no remote option
paragraphs: API withdrew remote proctoring for its core inspector programmes. The published position is that API 510, 570, 653, 1169 and 1184 are not available for remote testing. They run as computer-based examinations inside Prometric test centres. Remote proctoring through ProProctor remains available for other API examinations including 571, 577, 580 and 936, which is the source of most of the confusion when a sponsor plans a budget from memory.

For a sponsor this converts a scheduling problem into a logistics problem. The candidate travels to a Prometric centre, sits a seven-and-a-half-hour day, and is unavailable for at least one working day plus travel. On the Gulf Coast that is a short drive and a single hotel night. For crews working remote sites or offshore rotation it is a flight and two nights at $178 to $208 a day under the federal schedule.

Book the seat as soon as the application is approved. Prometric seat availability inside a three-week window is finite, and a reschedule costs $350 on top of whatever the missed travel already cost. This is the single most common way a sponsorship budget doubles, and it has nothing to do with the examination itself. Treat the confirmed seat as the deliverable, not the submitted application form.

sections.heading: The pay delta: what the data actually supports
paragraphs: Certification-filtered data and title-based aggregates tell different stories, and only one of them measures API 510 holders. Payscale reports a $131,000 average for people holding the certification across seventy-four respondents, updated February 2026. Salary.com's generic pressure vessel inspector title averages $62,807. ZipRecruiter's API 510 inspector title averages $54,939 nationally, which sits below the federal median for NDT specialists and should be read as title contamination rather than as market rate.

The defensible statement is narrower than the headline. Holding API 510 does not add $68,000 to a technician's salary. It qualifies that technician for a category of work, owner-user in-service inspection on operating pressure equipment, that pays in a higher band than general NDT, and the survey gap reflects the population that moved into that category. The certificate is the gate, not the raise on the other side of it.

For the US pay ladder this sits on top of, our page on [what NDT technicians actually make](/blog/how-much-do-ndt-technicians-make) decomposes the $78,350 federal median by certification level and by method. The [Gulf Coast comparison of code inspector and CWI pay](/blog/code-inspector-vs-cwi-salary-gulf-coast) then shows how per diem at $178 to $208 a day and turnaround overtime at one and a half times change the arithmetic again for anyone working shutdown seasons.

sections.heading: Bid eligibility is the value the salary tables miss
paragraphs: The commercial case for sponsoring an API 510 is rarely the individual's salary. It is the contract. Owner-user inspection programmes under API 510 require a certified inspector to set inspection intervals, evaluate results and authorise repairs and alterations on in-service vessels. A service company without one on the roster cannot bid that scope at all, and certified headcount appears on prequalification questionnaires as a hard pass-or-fail filter.

That converts the sponsorship from a retention cost into a market-access cost. One certified inspector opens a class of work. Two make the coverage credible across a turnaround. Three make it credible when somebody resigns in March. Contractors on the Gulf Coast size their certified headcount against the outage calendar rather than against the wage bill, because the wage bill follows the contract rather than the other way round.

The corollary is that the certificate depreciates fast when the work does not follow it. API requires at least twenty percent of working time over each three-year period to be spent supervising or performing pressure vessel inspection. A sponsored technician who returns to general NDT scopes will fail that requirement and lose the certification at the first recertification. Sponsor the people you can actually assign to vessel work.

sections.heading: The recertification cycle you are signing up for
paragraphs: API 510 recertifies every three years at $745 for members and $855 for non-members. Each cycle requires 24 Continuing Professional Development hours under ICP-PD-102, revised 15 September 2025. One CPD hour means at least fifty minutes of documented contact time, and activities shorter than fifty minutes earn nothing at all. A maximum of twelve hours carries over into the following cycle, so front-loading has a ceiling.

A six-year open-book web quiz sits on top of the three-year cycle, and the continued-experience requirement runs alongside both. Recertification applications open ninety days before expiry and close ninety days after, so the administrative window is six months wide and still easy to miss when a technician is on rotation. The ninety-day grace period after expiry is the last chance to act on a lapsing certificate.

Over nine years the recurring cost is real but modest: roughly $2,235 in member recertification fees plus seventy-two documented CPD hours per inspector. Tracking that across a crew on a spreadsheet is where programmes fail audits. Our [NDT personnel certification tracking module](/erp/ndt-personnel-certification-tracking) holds certification expiry dates, CPD hours and experience evidence against each technician record so the six-month window never arrives as a surprise.

sections.heading: Where API 510 is not worth it
paragraphs: Three situations make the sponsorship a waste. The first is a technician whose scope will not include in-service pressure vessels, because the twenty percent experience requirement goes unmet and the certificate lapses at the first recertification. The second is a fabrication-only shop, where new construction sits under the construction codes and the pressure-boundary inspection authority is the Authorized Inspector rather than an API 510 holder. The credential that pays there is a CWI.

The third is a candidate who does not yet meet the eligibility matrix. API requires one year of experience with an engineering or technology degree, two years with an associate degree, three years with a high school diploma and five years with no formal education, all acquired within the previous ten years under an authorised inspection agency. An application filed short of that fails on review, before the candidate ever sees the examination.

For crews in those situations the same money buys more as ASNT method certification. Adding phased array or radiography to an existing Level II changes what the crew can be dispatched to next week rather than in nine months, and it needs no external examination body. [Corporate NDT training](/corporate-ndt-training) covers that route for employers expanding an existing crew onto methods their clients are already requesting.

sections.heading: How to sponsor without burning a window
paragraphs: Work backwards from the application deadline rather than the examination date. For the September 2026 window that deadline was 3 July 2026; for the January 2027 window it is 29 October 2026. Confirm the eligibility documentation first, because an experience letter from an authorised inspection agency takes longer to obtain than the prep course takes to complete, and everything else fits inside the time that remains.

Then protect the study time in writing. A rotation schedule and a self-paced course are a poor combination unless the roster explicitly reserves hours for it. The most expensive outcome is not a failed examination; it is a candidate who never sits, forfeits the window, and repeats the application fee and the reschedule fee in the following cycle. Fix the roster before the purchase order for the course goes out.

Atlantis does not deliver API 510 training, and this page is independent guidance rather than a pitch for one. What we do run is [ASNT method training for US crews](/training-usa), [outsourced and interim Level III programme support](/consulting/asnt-level-iii-consulting-services), and [written practice development](/consulting/written-practice-development) for the employer-side documents governing who is certified to do what. If you are auditing an existing programme rather than staffing one, our [API 510 programme audit](/consulting/api-510-program-audit) covers that scope.

faq.q: How much does API 510 certification cost in total in 2026?
faq.a: Between $2,082 and $6,283 all-in for a sponsored candidate. API's examination and application fee is $875 for members and $1,125 for non-members. Prep runs $999 for a self-paced online course or $4,950 for a five-day instructor-led online course. One travel day to a Prometric centre adds $178 to $208 at federal per diem rates. Recertification then costs $745 every three years.

faq.q: Does API 510 actually raise a salary?
faq.a: It changes the category of work rather than adding a line to an existing payslip. Payscale's certification-filtered data reports $131,000 average for holders against $62,807 for the generic pressure vessel inspector title. The gap reflects the move into owner-user in-service inspection, which pays in a higher band than general NDT. Without that scope change the certificate lapses at the twenty percent experience requirement.

faq.q: How hard is the API 510 exam?
faq.a: It is a seven-and-a-half-hour day: 2.75 hours closed-book, a forty-five-minute lunch, then 3.75 hours open-book. There are 170 questions with 140 scored, split 110 closed-book and 60 open-book. The closed-book half is where candidates lose marks, particularly on the damage mechanisms in recommended practice 571. Open-book navigation speed matters more than depth of recall.

faq.q: Can a technician sit API 510 without a degree?
faq.a: Yes, with five years of experience in the design, fabrication, repair, operation or inspection of pressure vessels, of which at least one year must be supervising or performing inspection. A high school diploma cuts that to three years and a two-year associate degree to two years. All experience must fall within the previous ten years under an authorised inspection agency.

faq.q: What happens if an API 510 certification lapses?
faq.a: Recertification applications open ninety days before the expiry date and close ninety days after it, and the certificate requires 24 CPD hours plus continued inspection experience of at least twenty percent of working time across the three-year cycle. The ninety-day grace period after expiry is the final opportunity to act. Track the dates against each technician record rather than against a shared calendar.

faq.q: Is the oil and gas inspection market still hiring API inspectors in 2026?
faq.a: Federal projections for NDT specialists show one to two percent employment growth from 2024 to 2034 with 5,700 annual openings against 67,300 employed, so demand is replacement-driven rather than expanding. Code inspection sits on the scarce end of that market because the eligibility clock and the three-window examination calendar cap how fast new inspectors enter.

title: UR Z17 Approval Is Per-Society and Renews Every Three Years
description: IACS UR Z17 governs approval of thickness measurement, in-water survey and tightness testing firms: the document pack, office audit, witnessed demo and renewal.
h1: IACS Service Supplier Approval Under UR Z17: The Firm-Level Gate on Class Survey Work
answer: IACS UR Z17 requires any firm whose measurements a class surveyor relies on to hold that society's Certificate of Approval. The society reviews submitted documents, audits the office, and witnesses a practical demonstration before issuing. Thickness measurement firms renew every three years; the approval names one society and does not carry to another.
expansion: IACS Unified Requirement Z17 has been the mandatory procedure for approving service suppliers since 1997 and has been revised more than twenty times; Rev.22 was published in August 2025. It applies to firms whose results a class surveyor relies on when making decisions affecting classification or statutory certification. For four services — thickness measurement on ships and mobile offshore units, in-water survey by diver or ROV, ultrasonic tightness testing of closing appliances, and close-up survey by remote inspection techniques — Z17 states plainly that the provider must be approved and verified by that society. The route runs in one direction: submit the document pack listed in Section 5.1, pass an office audit that checks the firm is managed the way its documents describe, then complete a witnessed practical demonstration with a satisfactory report. The certificate that follows names the type and scope of service, and any limitation, in writing.
source: Full text of IACS UR Z17 'Procedural Requirements for Service Suppliers' Rev.9 (Türk Loydu copy) and Rev.15 (Roxtec copy), read clause by clause; the Rev.16 extract published by Indian Register of Shipping; ClassNK's published UR index confirming Rev.21 (Jan 2025) and Rev.22 (Aug 2025). Korean Register 'Guidance for Approval of Service Suppliers' GC-27-E (2022) for one society's own implementation. IACS PR 23 and MarineLink's report on the IACS thickness-measurement firm database. DNV-CP-0484 'Approval of service supplier scheme' and DNV's UTM service page. Lloyd's Register service supplier approval scheme page. IACS full membership (12 societies).

table.note: Clause numbers follow UR Z17 Rev.15 and later, where general requirements sit in Section 5 and certification in Section 6. Rev.9 and earlier carried the same content in Sections 4 and 5, so older audit checklists cite different numbers for identical requirements.

facets.q: Does an IACS UR Z17 approval from one class society work for another?
facets.a: No. The Certificate of Approval states that results performed under the supplier's system may be accepted by that Society's surveyors. A firm working ABS, DNV and Lloyd's Register tonnage holds three approvals. Societies share status through the IACS database required by PR 23, and Korean Register's guidance lets a demonstration verified by another IACS member satisfy that one element at initial audit — the certificate itself still comes from each society.

facets.q: How often does a thickness measurement approval have to be renewed?
facets.a: Every three years. UR Z17 sets five years as the renewal interval for most service supplier certificates but names thickness measurement firms as the exception, requiring renewal or endorsement at intervals not exceeding three years by verification that original conditions are maintained. Societies are free to go shorter and to require intermediate audits — DNV states that a surveyor audits every second year and again before the certificate expires.

facets.q: What is the witnessed practical demonstration, and can it be skipped?
facets.a: Certification is conditional on a practical demonstration of the specific service plus satisfactory reporting. At renewal audits, evidence of performance verified by a class surveyor since the previous audit satisfies the requirement instead. Korean Register's guidance adds that a firm approved for several methods demonstrates each scope separately and writes a service report for each, so one demonstration does not cover a four-method scope.

facets.q: Does UR Z17 require ISO 9001 certification?
facets.a: No. Z17 requires a documented system covering eight named elements: code of conduct, maintenance and calibration of equipment, training programmes, supervision and verification, recording and reporting, quality management of subsidiaries, agents and subcontractors, job preparation, and periodic review of procedures, complaints, corrective actions and document control. A documented system complying with the current ISO 9000 series and including those items is accepted, which is why most approved firms hold ISO 9001.

facets.q: Which service categories can an NDT firm hold Z17 approval for?
facets.a: Annex 1 runs to eighteen-plus categories. The ones an inspection company competes for are thickness measurement on ships and mobile offshore units, in-water survey by diver or ROV, ultrasonic tightness testing of closing appliances such as hatches and doors, close-up survey using remote inspection techniques, and examination of Ro-Ro bow, stern, side and inner doors. A firm gauging underwater, or by drone, needs the separate thickness measurement approval as well.

facets.q: What gets a Z17 approval cancelled?
facets.a: Six grounds are listed: the service was improperly carried out or the results improperly reported; a surveyor finds deficiencies and corrective action is not taken; the quality system was altered without written notification; a requested intermediate audit was not carried out; wilful acts or omissions; or deliberate misrepresentation. Expiry or cancellation of a parent company's approval automatically invalidates agents and subsidiaries certified under it.

sections.heading: The four services that make firm approval non-optional
paragraphs: UR Z17 splits service suppliers into statutory categories and categories that touch classification. For four of them the wording leaves no room: where the results of thickness measurement on ships or mobile offshore units, in-water survey by diver or ROV, ultrasonic tightness testing of closing appliances such as hatches and doors, or survey using remote inspection techniques are used by a surveyor in making decisions affecting classification, that provider must be approved and verified by that Society. No approval, no usable measurement.

The thickness measurement category carves out two exceptions and only two: non-ESP ships under 500 gross tonnage, and all fishing vessels. Everything else sits inside — bulk carriers, tankers, container ships, mobile offshore units. That is how an inspection firm which has quietly gauged small craft for years discovers, the first time a manager asks it to price a special survey, that the work it has been doing is not the work class will accept on the tonnage that pays.

Z17 is equally explicit about where approval is not compulsory. Low-location lighting inspection, sound-pressure measurement of public address and general alarm systems, noise-level measurement, coating system testing and examination of Ro-Ro bow, stern, side and inner doors do not require an approved supplier unless the flag Administration instructs otherwise. Read that list before assuming every marine service needs a certificate, then read the flag requirement, because flag can put the requirement back.

sections.heading: The document pack class reviews before an auditor books a flight
paragraphs: Section 5.1.1 fixes what goes to the society first, and the review happens on paper. The pack covers the company outline and management structure including any subsidiary to be included in the approval; the list of nominated agents, subsidiaries and subcontractors; the firm's experience in the specific service area; and a list of operators, technicians and inspectors documenting training and experience within that service area, with qualifications to recognised national, international or industry standards.

It continues with a description of the equipment used for the service sought, a guide for operators of that equipment, training programmes, checklists and record formats for recording results, and the quality manual or documented procedures covering the quality-system clause. Two items ambush firms: information on other activities that present a conflict of interest, and the record of customer claims and of corrective actions requested by certification bodies. Both are disclosures. Both are opened again at the audit.

The operator list is where packs run thin. A certificate number satisfies nobody — Z17 asks for training and experience documented alongside the qualification, and the general requirements demand a minimum of one year of tutored on-the-job training per operator. Rebuilding that evidence retrospectively is slow, which is why firms preparing for approval usually start with [written practice development](/consulting/written-practice-development) and fix the training file before a single document goes to class.

sections.heading: The office audit: what the auditor opens first
paragraphs: Once the documents are reviewed with a satisfactory result, the supplier is audited to establish that it is duly organised and managed in accordance with the submitted documents, and that it is capable of conducting the service. The test is consistency, not eloquence. An auditor who finds a beautifully written procedure that nobody in the field has read is looking at a firm that manages differently from how it documented itself, and that is the finding.

The general requirements give the auditor a fixed set of hooks. Supervision must exist for all services provided, with the responsible supervisor holding a minimum of two years of experience as an operator, technician or inspector within the activity — and where the supplier is one person, that person meets the supervisor requirements. Personnel records must contain age, formal education, training and experience for the services each person is approved for. Equipment records must contain maintenance and the results of calibration and verifications.

Two newer clauses catch modern firms. Subcontractors providing the services of the approved supplier must themselves meet the requirements of Section 5, so a firm that subcontracts crews inherits an audit obligation it rarely budgets for. And where computers acquire, process, record, report, store, assess or monitor data, the ability of the software to satisfy the intended application must be documented and confirmed before first use — commercial off-the-shelf word processors and databases excepted.

sections.heading: The witnessed demonstration, and what counts at renewal
paragraphs: Certification is conditional on a practical demonstration of the performance of the specific service, plus satisfactory reporting. This is the step firms underestimate, because it needs a real job on that society's classed tonnage with its surveyor present, and it is scheduled around the vessel, not around the applicant. Korean Register's published guidance records what the surveyor submits afterwards: pictorial evidence, a sample service report, the checklist and any non-conformity report.

Scope matters here more than anywhere else. Where a supplier holds several scopes — the guidance gives an NDT company approved for MT, PT, UT and RT as its example — an individual practical demonstration is conducted for each scope sought, with a service report written for each. A firm that plans one demonstration day for a four-method certificate has planned one day of four. Building demonstrable, method-specific procedures ahead of that is what [NDT technical procedure development](/consulting/ndt-technical-procedure-development) exists to do.

At renewal the burden changes shape. Evidence of performance verified by a class surveyor since the previous audit satisfies the demonstration requirement, which rewards firms that keep signed job reports filed by society. A firm that held an approval for three years and never worked that society's tonnage has no evidence to offer, and finds itself demonstrating from scratch — this time on a vessel it has to go and find.

sections.heading: Where SNT-TC-1A satisfies the operator requirement, and where it does not
paragraphs: Z17 makes the firm responsible for the qualification and training of its personnel to a recognised national, international or industry standard as applicable. For thickness measurement, Annex 1 names the responsible supervisor as qualified to a recognised industrial NDT standard with ISO 9712 Level II as the example, and operators as certified to a recognised standard with ISO 9712 Level I as the example, plus adequate knowledge of ship structures sufficient to select a representative position for each measurement.

In the United States the scheme firms actually run is employer-based certification under ASNT SNT-TC-1A. It meets the 'recognised national standard' wording only when the machinery behind it exists and is auditable: a written practice, general, specific and practical examinations, graded records, and the qualified Level III who signs all of it. Most small inspection firms have technicians with certificates and no Level III to stand behind them — which is the whole commercial case for [outsourced ASNT Level III consulting](/consulting/asnt-level-iii-consulting-services).

Societies also publish their own floor above the IACS example, and it can be higher. Korean Register's guidance requires thickness measurement operators certified to ISO 9712 Level II where the IACS example says Level I. Settle the accepted scheme in writing with the society before the office audit rather than after it, and treat the operator-level requirements as their own project — they are set out in detail on [UTM operator qualification for class approval](/consulting/utm-operator-qualification-class-approval).

sections.heading: Three years, not five: the renewal clock that catches TM firms
paragraphs: Renewal or endorsement of the Certificate is made at intervals not exceeding five years by verification through audits that approved conditions are maintained. Then Z17 adds the sentence that governs most NDT firms: for firms engaged in thickness measurements, renewal or endorsement is made at intervals not exceeding three years. Individual societies can require shorter intervals and can require intermediate audits on top.

Societies use that latitude. DNV states that a surveyor performs an audit every second year and again before the certificate expires, and that evidence of valid qualifications and training for service technicians is presented to the attending surveyor at the time the service is conducted. Korean Register's own guidance sets the renewal interval for its service supplier certificates at three years across the board. A firm holding several approvals is therefore managing several different clocks, not one.

There is a second expiry route that has nothing to do with the calendar. Where a category requires manufacturer authorisation, the certificate expires on expiry of the supplier's approval from the equipment manufacturer, whichever comes first, and the supplier must inform the society in due course. Failure to carry out a requested intermediate audit is itself listed as a ground for cancellation.

sections.heading: Approval is per-society, and it is also per-station
paragraphs: The Certificate of Approval states that the supplier's service operation system has been found satisfactory and that results performed in accordance with it may be accepted and utilised by the Society's surveyors. That sentence is the whole answer on transferability. IACS has twelve full members — ABS, Bureau Veritas, China Classification Society, Croatian Register of Shipping, DNV, Indian Register of Shipping, Korean Register, Lloyd's Register, ClassNK, Polish Register of Shipping, RINA and Türk Loydu — and each issues its own.

What crosses between societies is information and, in narrow circumstances, evidence. PR 23 obliges IACS members to report changes in the approval status of thickness measurement firms to a shared database, and to check that database before issuing or renewing a certificate. Korean Register's guidance allows a practical demonstration verified by another IACS member, confirmed against the quality system certification scheme, to satisfy that element at initial audit. The certificate still comes from each society separately.

Geography splits it further. Where several servicing stations are owned by a company, each station is assessed and approved, except under the specific clause covering a manufacturer's ISO 9000-certified system with effective control of nominated agents and subsidiaries. Expiry or cancellation of a parent company's approval automatically invalidates those agents and subsidiaries. Firms building multi-region maritime capability should plan the certificate map before the office map — a point [maritime NDT consulting](/consulting/maritime-ndt-consulting) work turns into a schedule.

sections.heading: How approval is lost, and what the shared database sees
paragraphs: Z17 lists six cancellation grounds and they are unforgiving: the service was improperly carried out or the results improperly reported; a surveyor finds deficiencies in the approved system and appropriate corrective action is not taken; alterations were made to the quality system without written notification; a requested intermediate audit was not carried out; wilful acts or omissions are ascertained; or deliberate misrepresentation has been made. The Society also reserves the right to inform the other IACS members.

One clause deserves separate attention because it reaches backwards. Where equipment is found not to conform to requirements, the Society assesses and records the validity of previous measuring results and takes appropriate action on the equipment affected. A gauge that fails a check does not just stop work — it puts already-issued reports into question. Per-instrument calibration and verification records, kept and available, are the only defence, and they are cheap compared to the alternative.

A cancelled supplier can apply for re-approval once it has corrected the non-conformities and the Society can confirm effective implementation of the corrective action. That is a full cycle again: documents, audit, demonstration. Firms doing offshore and mobile offshore unit work carry the same exposure across every society whose units they touch, which is why [offshore NDT consulting](/consulting/offshore-ndt-consulting) engagements start by auditing the evidence trail before anyone touches a procedure, and why [Level III exam oversight](/consulting/ndt-level-3-exam-oversight) is scheduled ahead of, not after, the renewal date.

faq.q: Do we need our own ASNT Level III on staff to get UR Z17 approval?
faq.a: Z17 requires a responsible supervisor qualified to a recognised NDT standard with two years of experience in the activity; it does not name a Level III. But where the firm runs an employer-based scheme under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, the operator certificates in the document pack only exist because a qualified Level III wrote the written practice and administered and graded the examinations. Firms without one on staff contract that role rather than skip it.

faq.q: Can we start class thickness work while the approval is in process?
faq.a: No. Where results are used by a surveyor in making decisions affecting classification, the provider must be approved and verified by that Society. Z17 also requires the report to include a copy of the Certificate of Approval, so there is no version of the deliverable that works before issue. Work done in the gap is not accepted and does not count as demonstration evidence.

faq.q: Does each of our branch offices need its own approval?
faq.a: Yes, with one exception. Where several servicing stations are owned by a given company, each station is assessed and approved, except where a manufacturer's ISO 9000-certified quality system with effective control of nominated agents and subsidiaries covers them under the specific clause. A second office does not inherit the first office's certificate by sharing a company name.

faq.q: What happens if class finds our thickness gauge out of calibration?
faq.a: Z17 requires the Society to assess and record the validity of previous measuring results when equipment is found not to conform, and to take appropriate action on the equipment affected. That reaches into reports already issued and accepted. Per-serial-number calibration and verification records, with the reference block identified, are what limits the damage to the instrument rather than the file.

faq.q: How long does the whole approval sequence take?
faq.a: The order is fixed — document review, office audit, witnessed demonstration, certificate — and the demonstration is the constraint, because it needs a live job on that society's classed tonnage with its surveyor present. Firms that assemble the document pack, personnel records and training evidence before submitting clear the review in one round instead of three, which is usually where the calendar is won or lost.

title: UTM Operator Files Fail Class Audits Before Procedures Do
description: What a UTM operator must hold for class thickness work: NDT certification, ship-structure knowledge, vision, gauge calibration and the signed TM report.
h1: Qualifying UTM Operators for Class Thickness Measurement Work
answer: Class requires each ultrasonic thickness operator to hold certification to a recognised NDT standard — ISO 9712, or an SNT-TC-1A employer certification signed by a Level III — plus documented ship-structure knowledge, current annual vision, and a gauge calibration record. The attending surveyor verifies the technician file on the job, and the TM report carries the operator's qualification.
expansion: A class thickness measurement job has two gates. The firm-level gate is IACS UR Z17 approval, held by the company and audited on a cycle. The operator-level gate is the technician file, and that one is checked on the job by the attending surveyor rather than once every three years by an auditor. Z17 Annex 1 requires operators carrying out the measurements to be certified to a recognised national or international industrial standard, with ISO 9712 Level I named as the example, and to hold adequate knowledge of ship structures sufficient to select a representative position for each measurement. The general requirements add a minimum of one year of tutored on-the-job training, personnel records showing age, formal education, training and experience, and an equipment record containing maintenance and the results of calibration and verifications. The surveyor signs each separate job, and the report prints the operator's qualification as a field.
source: IACS UR Z17 Annex 1 Section 1 and general requirements 5.2.2 to 5.2.6, read in the Rev.15 and Rev.16 texts. Korean Register 'Guidance for Approval of Service Suppliers' GC-27-E (2022), Appendix Part A Section 1, for a society's own operator level. The ESP thickness-measurement report forms reproduced at imorules.com (Annex 8A, double-side skin bulk carriers) for the report field list. IACS common structural rules definition of substantial corrosion. ISO 9712 validity and near-vision provisions, including the ISO 9712:2022 colour-vision change. ASNT SNT-TC-1A 2024 recertification and vision provisions. DNV's UTM service page (PEGASUS mandatory for FIS vessels from 1 July 2017) and DNV-CP-0484.

table.note: Where equipment is later found not to conform to requirements, UR Z17 requires the society to assess and record the validity of previous measuring results. A failed gauge check therefore reaches backwards into reports already issued, which makes the per-instrument record the highest-value page in the file.

facets.q: Is SNT-TC-1A UT Level II enough to gauge hull thickness for class?
facets.a: It satisfies the operator requirement where the society accepts an employer-based national scheme and the machinery behind the certificate is auditable: a written practice, general, specific and practical examinations, graded records, and a qualified Level III signature. It is not enough on its own. Korean Register's published guidance names ISO 9712 Level II for thickness measurement operators, so confirm the accepted scheme with each society in writing before the job.

facets.q: What does 'adequate knowledge of ship structures' actually mean in the file?
facets.a: UR Z17 ties it to a task: the operator must know enough about ship structures to select a representative position for each measurement. Auditors read that as evidence, not assertion — a structures training record, an assignment log naming vessel types and the members gauged, and a documented training plan covering minimum rule requirements, recognition of corrosion damage, buckling and deteriorated coatings. A generic UT certificate proves none of it.

facets.q: How often does a UTM operator need a vision test?
facets.a: Annually. ISO 9712 requires near-vision acuity verified before certification and annually thereafter, permitting a minimum of Jaeger number 1 or Times Roman N4.5 at not less than 30 cm, with one or both eyes, corrected or uncorrected. SNT-TC-1A's 2024 edition sets Jaeger number 2 annually. Colour vision moved to a five-year cycle under ISO 9712:2022 and sits at five-year intervals in SNT-TC-1A 2024.

facets.q: What calibration evidence does the surveyor expect at the gangway?
facets.a: An equipment record containing maintenance and the results of calibration and verifications for the specific instrument being used, tied to its serial number, plus the function check performed on the day against an identified reference block. Z17 also requires the pulse-echo multiple-echo single-crystal technique on coated surfaces; single-echo instruments are limited to uncoated surfaces that have been cleaned and ground.

facets.q: What must the thickness measurement report contain?
facets.a: The class TM report form carries the firm's name, the society that certified it, the certificate number and validity dates, and the operator's qualification, alongside strake and plate position, structural member, original thickness, gauged readings port and starboard, diminution in millimetres and per cent, and the maximum allowable diminution. It ends with the place of measurement, the firm's stamp, and the attending surveyor's name and signature.

facets.q: Does the surveyor have to witness every job?
facets.a: UR Z17 Annex 1 requires the supplier to have the surveyor's verification of each separate job, documented in the report by the attending surveyor's signature. That is per job, not per certificate cycle. It means the technician file is exposed continuously rather than at audit, and it is why an out-of-date vision record or an expired certificate surfaces at the gangway rather than in an office three years later.

sections.heading: What a UTM operator must actually hold
paragraphs: IACS UR Z17 Annex 1, Section 1 sets two personnel requirements for firms engaged in thickness measurements. The responsible supervisor is qualified according to a recognised national or international industrial NDT standard, with ISO 9712 Level II given as the example. The operators carrying out the measurements are certified to a recognised national or international industrial standard, with ISO 9712 Level I as the example, and hold adequate knowledge of ship structures sufficient to select a representative position for each measurement.

Those are minima with a floor that societies can raise, and they do. Korean Register's published guidance for approval of service suppliers requires thickness measurement operators certified to ISO 9712 Level II — the level IACS names for the supervisor. A technician file built to the IACS example clears one society and fails another, on the same vessel type, doing the same work. Confirm the accepted scheme and level, in writing, per society, before the technician is assigned.

The general requirements add the part firms forget. Operators, technicians and inspectors must have had a minimum of one year of tutored on-the-job training, and where internal training is impossible a programme of external training is considered acceptable. Supervision must be provided for all services, and the responsible supervisor must have a minimum of two years of experience as an operator within the activity for which the supplier is approved.

sections.heading: Where SNT-TC-1A sits inside the class requirement
paragraphs: ASNT SNT-TC-1A is a recommended practice for employer-based certification, and it is the scheme almost every US inspection firm actually runs. Class does not name it in Annex 1 — the examples are ISO 9712 and the withdrawn EN 473 — but the requirement is written as 'a recognised national or international industrial standard', which leaves room for a national employer-based practice provided the firm can show the standard behind the certificate.

Showing it means producing the apparatus, not the card. A written practice that identifies the requirements for control and administration of training, examination and certification. Documented training hours and experience per method. General, specific and practical examinations that were prepared, administered and graded. Records that correlate to the examination sat. And the qualified Level III whose signature makes the certificate valid — the reason [written practice development](/consulting/written-practice-development) and [Level III exam oversight](/consulting/ndt-level-3-exam-oversight) are the first two workstreams in any class-approval project.

SNT-TC-1A also makes provision for limited certification, which is how UT thickness measurement is commonly certified — a Level II restricted to thickness gauging. That is legitimate when the limitation is described in the written practice and printed on the certification record. It becomes a finding when the certificate says Level II UT without limitation and the technician has only ever been trained and examined on thickness. The routes and their boundaries are set out on [ASNT certification](/asnt-certification).

sections.heading: The ship-structure knowledge element nobody documents
paragraphs: The phrase in Annex 1 is doing real work: adequate knowledge of ship structures sufficient to select a representative position for each measurement. A thickness reading taken 200 millimetres from where class expected it is a different number. The operator is being asked to make a structural judgement in the moment, and Z17 makes the firm responsible for evidencing that the operator can.

Evidence looks like a training plan and a training record. Z17's companion categories spell out the expected content — minimum rule requirements for relevant ship and unit types, the ship's or unit's structure including internal structure, recognition of corrosion damage, buckling, cracking and deteriorated coatings, and use of the reporting system. Firms that document ultrasonic competence and nothing else have half a file, and the missing half is the half a class auditor can find in ten minutes.

This is the element that separates a general industrial UT technician from a UTM operator. The certificate transfers; the structural knowledge does not. A firm moving into class work from refinery or fabrication inspection needs a deliberate structures training programme with dated records per operator — the kind of gap [maritime NDT consulting](/consulting/maritime-ndt-consulting) is engaged to close before the first witnessed job rather than during it.

sections.heading: The witnessed job: the surveyor signs each separate report
paragraphs: UR Z17 Annex 1 requires the supplier to have the surveyor's verification of each separate job, documented in the report by the attending surveyor's signature. That single clause changes the risk profile of the whole programme. Firm-level approval is audited on a three-year cycle; the technician file is inspected every time a surveyor attends. Expired certificates, stale vision records and unnamed supervisors surface at the gangway.

DNV states the expectation directly for its own scheme: evidence of valid qualifications and training for service technicians is presented to attending surveyors at the time the service is conducted. In practice that means the crew travels with the file, not with a promise that the file exists at head office. Firms that keep a per-technician evidence pack — certificate, vision record, OJT log, structures training record — clear the check without a phone call.

The demonstration requirement at approval works the same way. Certification is conditional on a practical demonstration of the specific service plus satisfactory reporting, and where a firm seeks several scopes each is demonstrated separately with its own service report. At renewal, evidence of performance verified by a class surveyor since the previous audit satisfies the requirement — which rewards a firm that has kept its signed reports filed by society and by date.

sections.heading: Gauge calibration evidence, per instrument
paragraphs: Z17 requires the supplier to keep a record of the equipment used, available on request, containing information on maintenance and the results of calibration and verifications. The word that matters is 'results'. A calibration certificate stapled to a folder is a document; the audit wants the values, the dates, the reference used, and the decision that followed. Records are kept per instrument, tied to the serial number that appears on the report.

Annex 1 also constrains the instrument itself. On coated surfaces, instruments using the pulsed echo technique — oscilloscope, or digital using multiple echo, single crystal technique — are required. Single echo instruments are permitted only on uncoated surfaces that have been cleaned and ground. A firm gauging over coating with a single-echo gauge is producing readings class will not accept, regardless of how well the technician is certified.

The consequence clause is the one to plan around. Where equipment is found not to conform to requirements, the Society assesses and records the validity of previous measuring results and takes appropriate action on the equipment affected. That is retrospective exposure across every report that instrument produced since its last good check. Daily function checks against an identified reference block, recorded and retained, are what bound the blast radius to one day rather than one year.

sections.heading: Vision, recertification and keeping the file current
paragraphs: Under ISO 9712 the certificate is valid for five years, and near-vision acuity is verified before certification and annually thereafter — a minimum of Jaeger number 1 or Times Roman N4.5 or equivalent at not less than 30 cm, with one or both eyes, corrected or uncorrected. Colour vision moved to a five-year demonstration under the 2022 edition. Under SNT-TC-1A's 2024 edition the recommended maximum recertification interval is five years for Levels I, II and III, near vision is Jaeger number 2 annually, and colour contrast is examined at initial certification and at five-year intervals.

Annual is the operative word for vision in both schemes, and it is the single most common expired item in a UTM technician file. A vision test taken thirteen months ago invalidates the technician for the job in front of the surveyor. Firms that batch vision testing on a fixed calendar month, and diary it, remove the most frequent gangway failure at essentially no cost.

Recertification is a scheduling problem, not a technical one. Five-year certificate cycles, three-year firm approval cycles and annual vision cycles run on different clocks, and none of them align. A single register showing every technician's certificate expiry, vision date, OJT completion and structures training, reviewed monthly, is what an [outsourced ASNT Level III](/consulting/asnt-level-iii-consulting-services) maintains for firms that do not have one internally — and the boundaries of that role are set out on [what an outside Level III can and cannot do](/consulting/outside-ndt-level-3-can-and-cannot-do).

sections.heading: The TM report class expects: members, diminution, percentages
paragraphs: The thickness measurement report is a controlled form, not a free-text deliverable. The ESP report formats carry the name of the firm performing the measurement, the society that certified the firm, the certificate number, the certificate validity dates, and the qualification of the operator — printed identity fields that expose the whole approval chain on the first page. A firm without a certificate cannot complete the header, which is the point.

The measurement body identifies structure before it reports numbers: strake position, plate position and structural member, then original thickness in millimetres, gauged readings port and starboard, and diminution port and starboard expressed in both millimetres and per cent, against the maximum allowable diminution. Place of measurement is recorded and referenced to structural sketches. The report closes with the firm's official stamp and the surveyor's name and signature.

Those percentages carry the decision. IACS defines substantial corrosion as an extent of corrosion such that assessment of the corrosion pattern indicates wastage in excess of 75 per cent of allowable margins but within acceptable limits — the trigger for extended measurement at subsequent surveys. Reporting raw thickness without the diminution calculation moves that assessment onto the surveyor's desk, and firms that do it get asked to resubmit. Building the calculation into the reporting template is a one-off engineering job with a permanent return.

sections.heading: Why the technician file fails the audit before the procedure does
paragraphs: Procedures are written once, reviewed by a Level III, and improve with each revision. Technician files decay continuously — certificates expire, people leave, vision tests lapse, a new hire arrives with a certificate from a previous employer that the current firm has never verified. The asymmetry is why audit findings cluster in personnel records even at firms with excellent documented procedures.

Z17 tells the auditor exactly what to look for, which makes the finding easy to write. Personnel records shall contain information on age, formal education, training and experience for the services for which each person is approved. Four fields. Most firms hold one — the certificate — and assume the rest is implied. The tutored on-the-job training year is the second most common gap, because nobody logged it while it was happening.

Fix the file first, then the procedure. A firm-wide personnel record rebuilt to the four Z17 fields, plus an OJT log, structures training record, vision register and per-instrument calibration file, removes the majority of realistic findings before class sees the door. The procedures that sit on top of it are then worth writing properly, which is what [NDT technical procedure development](/consulting/ndt-technical-procedure-development) delivers, and the firm-level gate those procedures serve is covered on [IACS UR Z17 service supplier approval](/consulting/iacs-service-supplier-approval).

faq.q: Can a technician certified by a previous employer gauge for us immediately?
faq.a: Not without verification. SNT-TC-1A certification is employer-based, so the certificate belongs to the issuing employer's written practice, not to the individual. The new employer either accepts prior certification under documented rules in its own written practice and evidences it, or examines and certifies the technician itself. Class will read the personnel record as your firm's record, and the four required fields have to be yours.

faq.q: Do UTM operators need to be Level II, or is Level I enough?
faq.a: UR Z17 Annex 1 names ISO 9712 Level I as the example for operators and Level II for the responsible supervisor. Individual societies raise it — Korean Register's guidance requires operators certified to ISO 9712 Level II. Because the requirement is set per society and printed on the report as the operator's qualification, the practical answer is to build to Level II and confirm the accepted level in writing before mobilising.

faq.q: What reporting software does class require for UTM?
faq.a: It is set by the society, not by IACS. DNV made its PEGASUS tool mandatory for UTM reports on FIS-notation vessels from 1 July 2017. Others accept the ESP report formats completed to the required fields. Confirm the tool and template before quoting a job, because report rejection after demobilisation costs more than the gauging did.

faq.q: Does a firm doing underwater or drone thickness measurement need separate approval?
faq.a: Yes. UR Z17 requires a firm carrying out in-water close-up survey by ROV to hold the in-water survey approval, and a supplier undertaking thickness measurements as part of a remote inspection technique service to hold the separate approval as a firm engaged in thickness measurements on ships. The approvals stack; one does not absorb the other.

faq.q: How do we prove ship-structure knowledge for a technician hired from industrial inspection?
faq.a: With a documented structures training programme and a dated record per operator: minimum rule requirements for the ship types worked, internal and underwater structure, recognition of corrosion damage, buckling, cracking and deteriorated coatings, use of the reporting system, then a supervised assignment log. The UT certificate proves the method; only the training and assignment records prove the operator can choose a representative position.

title: NAVSEA 271 Makes SNT-TC-1A a Mandatory Minimum, Not a Guideline
description: NAVSEA T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 for shipyard NDT: written practice, three-year certifications, Examiner-approved procedures and where it goes beyond SNT-TC-1A.
h1: NDT Requirements for Navy and Navy-Contract Shipyard Work
answer: NAVSEA T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 Revision 1 governs RT, MT, PT, UT, ET and VT on Navy work. Personnel are certified under the activity's own written practice developed per ASNT SNT-TC-1A — but 271 invokes SNT-TC-1A as mandatory minimums, caps operator and inspector certification at three years, bans recertification without examination, and prohibits transferring certifications between activities.
expansion: NAVSEA Technical Publication T9074-AS-GIB-010/271, Revision 1 dated 11 September 2014, is the governing NDT document for Navy and Navy-contract work. It covers radiographic, magnetic particle, liquid penetrant, ultrasonic, eddy current and visual testing, and contains the minimum requirements necessary to qualify NDT personnel, procedures and equipment. It does not contain acceptance criteria — those come from the applicable drawing, specification, contract or order — and it does not cover underwater NDT, which is performed as specified in NAVSEA S0600-AA-PRO-070. Personnel are certified in accordance with the employing activity's written practice, developed as required by ASNT SNT-TC-1A. The sentence that follows is the one that reshapes a commercial NDT programme: SNT-TC-1A, as modified by 271, is invoked as mandatory minimum requirements and shall not be considered recommendations or guidelines. A copy of the written practice goes to the Government inspector on request.
source: NAVSEA Technical Publication T9074-AS-GIB-010/271 Revision 1, 11 September 2014 (public release, distribution unlimited) — Chapters 1 and 2 read in full, including 1.5.5 to 1.5.7, 1.6.1 to 1.6.10.2, 1.7.1 to 1.7.4, 1.8 and the Chapter 2 referenced-document list. ASNT's Naval Shipbuilders NDT Level III certification page for the examination format and eligibility. ASNT SNT-TC-1A 2024 edition recertification and vision provisions for the comparison. Published titles for NAVSEA Standard Item 009-12, S9074-AQ-GIB-010/248 and T9074-AD-GIB-010/1688. ASNT NDT Level III examination page for Basic and Method exam formats.
