table.note: Federal cells quote or paraphrase the published CFR text. AAR requirements are described from published AAR MSRP material; the full specifications are proprietary and are supplied to certified facilities. Confirm the current edition with AAR before relying on any element description.

facets.q: What does 49 CFR 179.7 require of a tank car repair shop?
facets.a: No tank car facility may manufacture, repair, inspect, test, qualify or maintain tank cars without an AAR-approved quality assurance programme. That programme must include the qualification requirements of personnel performing non-destructive inspections and tests, procedures for evaluating the inspection and test technique employed, calibration procedures, record maintenance and employee training. The NDT personnel clause is explicit federal text, not an AAR preference.

facets.q: Does AAR M-1003 require an NDT Level III?
facets.a: M-1003 is built on 24 quality assurance elements, and personnel qualification is one of the technical approval elements an auditor examines alongside publications, subcontracting and demonstration capability. AAR tank car facility certification records call for the name of the facility's NDT Level III and the expiration date of that certification by method. A blank there is a visible gap on the certification record.

facets.q: Which welds does 180.509 single out for structural integrity inspection?
facets.a: All transverse fillet welds greater than 0.25 inch within 4 feet of the bottom longitudinal centerline, and the termination points of longitudinal fillet welds in that same zone. Tank shell butt welds within 2 feet of the bottom centerline are included unless the owner demonstrates by analysis that structural integrity is maintained. A procedure that does not address that zone by name does not cover the inspection.

facets.q: Who can operate rail flaw detection equipment under 213.237?
facets.a: The rule states that the person assigned to operate the rail defect detection equipment must be a qualified operator, with demonstrated proficiency for each type of equipment operated. The per-type wording matters: proficiency on one detector car or hand-held unit does not transfer to another. Frequency obligations run against class of track, annual tonnage and service failure rate targets rather than a single calendar interval.

facets.q: Which NDT methods are permitted for tank car requalification?
facets.a: 180.509 permits dye penetrant, radiographic examination, magnetic particle, ultrasonic testing, and visual inspection assisted by magnifiers, fiberscopes, borescopes or machine vision technology. Acceptance criteria sit in 180.511. Choosing among them is a technique decision tied to weld geometry, access and coating condition — which is exactly the decision a Level III is qualified to make and document.

facets.q: How does an M-1003 audit differ from a Nadcap audit?
facets.a: Both are industry-body accreditation audits of a supplier's quality system, both include on-site assessment, and both examine NDT personnel qualification as a discrete element. M-1003 governs rail supply under AAR's 24 elements; Nadcap AC7114 governs aerospace NDT under prime-driven checklists with tighter method-specific audit criteria. Firms preparing for the aerospace equivalent use /consulting/nadcap-ac7114-audit-readiness.

sections.heading: Why Chicago concentrates rail inspection demand
paragraphs: Chicago is the interchange point for six of the seven North American Class I railroads, moving more than 500 freight trains a day and roughly a quarter of the nation's rail freight. The Belt Railway of Chicago — the largest switching terminal railroad in the country, co-owned by BNSF, Canadian National, CPKC, CSX, Norfolk Southern and Union Pacific — classifies more than 8,400 cars a day at Clearing Yard, a 786-acre facility running about 5.5 miles along the Chicago and Bedford Park boundary just south of Midway, with over 250 miles of track.

The intermodal footprint is separate and equally large. BNSF's Logistics Park Chicago near Joliet and Union Pacific's Global IV are among the biggest intermodal facilities in the world, and the region has handled millions of container lifts a year. The CREATE Program, a public-private partnership launched in 2003, has been rebuilding the region's rail geometry across roughly 70 capital projects and supports tens of thousands of jobs.

What that density produces for an inspection contractor is volume and proximity. Cars are inspected, repaired and requalified where they already are, and Chicago is where they already are. The demand is steady rather than campaign-driven, which changes how a shop has to staff its certification programme — continuously, not around a turnaround.

sections.heading: The federal sentence that decides whether the shop can operate
paragraphs: 49 CFR 179.7 is short and absolute. No tank car facility may manufacture, repair, inspect, test, qualify or maintain tank cars unless it operates under an AAR-approved quality assurance programme. That programme has to ensure finished products conform to specification, detect nonconformities and prevent recurrence, and it has to include calibration procedures, record maintenance systems, and training of employees on the programme's procedures.

Inside that list sits the clause this page exists for: the programme must include the qualification requirements of personnel performing non-destructive inspections and tests, together with procedures for evaluating the inspection and test technique employed. Those are two separate obligations — who is qualified, and how the technique itself is validated — and shops commonly document the first while leaving the second implicit.

The consequence of failing that element is not a finding to be closed at leisure. Without an approved programme the facility is not permitted to perform the work at all. That is why the personnel qualification element gets read early in an audit and why a shop with no identifiable certifying authority has a structural problem rather than a paperwork problem. The role that fills it is described at /consulting/asnt-level-iii-consulting-services.

sections.heading: AAR M-1003 and where the Level III surfaces on the record
paragraphs: M-1003, carried in AAR's Manual of Standards and Recommended Practices Section J, is the quality assurance specification that certified rail suppliers operate under. It comprises 24 elements requiring a documented quality assurance system built from policies, procedures, inspection and test plans, work instructions and quality records, plus technical approval elements covering publications, personnel qualifications, subcontracting and demonstration capabilities. The administrative provisions cover application, on-site audits, maintaining certification and handling changes.

Personnel qualification is a technical approval element, which means an auditor assesses it against the technical work the facility performs rather than against a generic training checklist. For NDT, the evidence expected is a written practice, training and experience records traceable to it, examination results, vision examinations, and certifications signed by a qualified Level III. AAR's tank car facility certification records call for the name of the facility's NDT Level III and the expiration date of that certification by method.

That last detail is worth sitting with. The Level III's name is on the certification record itself, per method. Not on an internal file, not in a training matrix — on the record the auditor works from. Shops that have never had that name filled in for a method they actually perform are carrying a visible discrepancy, and the fix begins with the document at /consulting/written-practice-development.

sections.heading: 180.509: the weld zones an auditor will name
paragraphs: Requalification of specification tank cars under 180.509 breaks into visual inspection internally and externally, structural integrity inspection, thickness testing, and service equipment inspection, on intervals reaching to ten years. The structural integrity inspection is the one that turns into an NDT scope, and the rule is specific about geometry rather than leaving it to judgement.

It names all transverse fillet welds greater than 0.64 cm — a quarter inch — within 121.92 cm, four feet, of the bottom longitudinal centerline, and the termination points of longitudinal fillet welds within that same zone. Tank shell butt welds within two feet of the bottom centerline are included unless the owner demonstrates through analysis that structural integrity will be maintained without it. Permitted methods are dye penetrant, radiographic examination, magnetic particle, ultrasonic testing, and visual inspection using magnifiers, fiberscopes, borescopes or machine vision technology, with acceptance criteria carried in 180.511.

A procedure that names a method and an acceptance standard without addressing that zone, the coating that covers it, the access constraints under a jacketed car, and the flaw orientation those welds produce is not a procedure the shop can defend. Writing it against the geometry rather than against the method is the distinction, and it is the deliverable at /consulting/ndt-technical-procedure-development.

sections.heading: Rail flaw detection and the qualified operator requirement
paragraphs: Track-side work runs under a different rule with a similar logic. 49 CFR 213.237 governs internal rail inspection, setting frequencies against class of track and accumulated tonnage — Class 4 and 5 track not exceeding 370 days or 30 million gross tons between inspections, whichever comes first, with Class 3 track carrying passengers or hazardous materials held to the same interval and other Class 3 track running to an annual or 30 mgt cycle. The rule also sets service failure rate targets per year per mile that the inspection programme has to hold.

The personnel clause is direct: the person assigned to operate the rail defect detection equipment must be a qualified operator, with demonstrated proficiency for each type of equipment operated. Per type. A technician proficient on one detector configuration is not thereby qualified on another, and the demonstration record has to show the distinction.

For contractors running ultrasonic rail testing in the Chicago terminal district, that requirement sits alongside — not inside — SNT-TC-1A certification. A Level II in ultrasonics is not automatically a qualified operator under 213.237, and a qualified operator is not automatically certified in UT. Keeping both records, separately and currently, is what survives a railroad's contractor audit.

sections.heading: Wheel, axle and component lines
paragraphs: Wheel shops, axle lines and casting inspection run on customer specifications layered over the shop's M-1003 quality system. The methods are familiar — magnetic particle on axles and journals, ultrasonic through-transmission and shear wave on axle bodies, visual and dimensional on wheels — and the audit exposure is concentrated in two places: whether the technique was demonstrated on representative geometry, and whether the acceptance criteria trace to a controlled source.

The recurring finding is criteria drift. A shop inspects to numbers printed on a customer drawing, and when the auditor asks which procedure those numbers came from, there is no procedure. The drawing changed two revisions ago and nobody reconciled the inspection instruction. That is a Level III control failure, not an operator failure, and it is corrected by writing the criteria into a controlled procedure with a revision history.

Calibration records are the second exposure. Reference blocks, notched standards and reference photographs all need traceability and controlled storage, and every method procedure has to state which standard it calibrates against. Shops keeping that data in spreadsheets find retrieval during an audit painful; holding certifications, calibration due dates and procedure revisions in one auditable system is what /erp addresses.

sections.heading: What an outsourced Level III delivers to a Chicago shop
paragraphs: The engagement maps directly onto the audit elements. The Level III authors or repairs the written practice covering each method the shop performs. He builds and administers general, specific and practical examinations, grades them, and signs the certifications — putting a real name against each method on the certification record. He approves the NDT procedures against the weld zones 180.509 names and the acceptance criteria 180.511 carries, and he validates the technique the way 179.7 requires.

During the audit he is the person who answers how a Level II was qualified in a given method, why a technique was selected for a given geometry, and what changed at the last procedure revision. Shops that keep their technicians but need the certifying and examining authority engage the narrower scope at /consulting/ndt-level-3-exam-oversight.

What he does not do is take over production decisions, sign for work he did not review, or certify people the shop has not actually trained to the practice. Those boundaries are set out plainly at /consulting/outside-ndt-level-3-can-and-cannot-do, and stating them in the quality manual is itself an audit-defensible position.

sections.heading: Timing the certification clock against the audit clock
paragraphs: Certification programmes fail on dates more than on content. Vision examinations expire annually. Method certifications carry recertification intervals set by the written practice. Procedures carry revision dates that have to track code and specification changes. Auditors sample those dates because they are objective, and a single expired near-vision record on a technician who worked last week is a finding that needs no debate.

The build sequence has a floor. Examinations can be scheduled quickly; documented training hours and experience cannot be created after the fact. A shop preparing for an M-1003 audit or a tank car facility certification review needs the personnel gap identified early enough that technicians short on documented training can complete it legitimately. Method training toward that gap sits at /corporate-ndt-training, and the wider certification landscape technicians move through is mapped at /asnt-certification.

Atlantis provides outsourced ASNT Level III coverage, written practice development, NDT procedure development and examination oversight for tank car shops, freight car facilities, component lines and rail flaw detection contractors across the Chicago terminal district. Contractors working the pipeline side of the same NDT market will find the parallel page at /consulting/pipeline-ndt-consulting-tulsa. Positioning is affordable, accessible and fully customisable to the methods a shop actually performs — scope and a quote on request at /contact.

faq.q: Does a tank car repair shop legally need an NDT Level III?
faq.a: 49 CFR 179.7 requires the facility's AAR-approved quality assurance programme to include the qualification requirements of personnel performing non-destructive inspections and tests. It does not print the words 'Level III', but AAR tank car facility certification records call for the name of the facility's NDT Level III and the expiration date by method, which is where the requirement becomes concrete.

faq.q: Can an outsourced Level III be named on the AAR certification record?
faq.a: SNT-TC-1A places certifying authority with a qualified Level III operating under the employer's written practice and does not require full-time employment. The arrangement has to be documented in the written practice and the quality programme, and the named person needs to be available during the on-site audit to answer for the certifications and procedures he signed.

faq.q: Is an SNT-TC-1A Level II the same as a qualified operator under 213.237?
faq.a: No. 213.237 requires that the person operating rail defect detection equipment be a qualified operator with demonstrated proficiency for each type of equipment operated. That is a task-and-equipment qualification held against the track safety standard. Method certification under SNT-TC-1A is separate. Contractors doing both need both records maintained independently.

faq.q: How is an M-1003 audit different from an ISO 9001 audit?
faq.a: ISO 9001 assesses a general management system. M-1003 assesses a rail-specific quality assurance system against 24 elements including technical approval areas — publications, personnel qualifications, subcontracting and demonstration capabilities — with an on-site audit tied to the technical work the facility actually performs. NDT personnel qualification is examined as a discrete technical element rather than folded into competence generally.

faq.q: What does a Chicago engagement start with?
faq.a: A comparison of the current written practice against the methods the shop performs and the certification record AAR holds, plus a sample of technician files. That read shows within a day whether the gap is a document repair, a full rebuild, or an examination campaign, and it sets the realistic timeline against the next audit date. Scope and a quote follow, on request at /contact.

title: Wichita Aerospace NDT: Clear AC7114 Without a Staff Level III
description: Wichita's 350-supplier aerostructures base runs on Nadcap AC7114 and NAS 410. How an outsourced ASNT Level III signs the written practice and clears the audit.
h1: Aerospace NDT Consulting in Wichita: Getting a Tier-2 Shop Through AC7114
answer: Wichita's tier-2 shops sell into Spirit AeroSystems, Textron Aviation and Bell's V-280 fuselage assembly line, and each buyer flows down Nadcap AC7114. Accreditation turns on a written practice signed by a qualified Level III, method procedures carrying that same approval, and personnel files built to NAS 410 Revision 5. Atlantis supplies that Level III under contract.
expansion: Wichita is the densest aerostructures supply base in the United States: roughly 350 supplier firms in the greater Wichita region feeding fuselage and flight-deck production, Textron Aviation's Cessna and Beechcraft programs, Airbus's A220 pylon work, and Bell's Wichita Assembly Center building V-280 fuselages. Almost none of those shops buy NDT from outside — they run penetrant, magnetic particle and ultrasonic in-house because the primes require in-process inspection. That makes each of them an NDT employer under NAS 410, which requires a named Responsible Level 3 to author the written practice, approve every method procedure, and administer qualification examinations. Boeing's 2025 acquisition of Spirit AeroSystems reset supplier quality flowdown across the region, and Nadcap AC7114 accreditation is the yardstick the reset is measured against. An outsourced Level III fills the role for the shops that cannot justify a full-time one — the common case between twenty and a hundred and fifty employees.
source: Verified against: Nadcap AC7114 audit criteria and the Performance Review Institute's 30-day self-audit requirement; NAS 410 Revision 5 (September 2020), including the 75%/100% experience gates for specific and practical examinations; FAA AC 65-31B, Training, Qualification, and Certification of Nondestructive Inspection Personnel; 14 CFR 145.155, Inspection personnel requirements; Greater Wichita Partnership aerospace industry profile (supplier counts, NIAR, NCAT, Eisenhower National and Jabara Airport tenants); Spirit AeroSystems corporate record on the Boeing acquisition and the Airbus transfer of Wichita A220 pylon production; Bell Textron FLRAA facility announcements naming the Wichita Assembly Center; Kaman Composite Structures FAA Part 145 certification at Wichita; Learjet final delivery, March 2022.

table.note: Nadcap accreditation and a prime's own approved-processor listing are separate gates. Clearing AC7114 does not by itself place a Wichita shop on a customer's approved processor list, and losing the customer approval does not revoke the Nadcap certificate. Both have to be held at once.

facets.q: Does a Wichita tier-2 shop need Nadcap accreditation if it only runs in-process penetrant?
facets.a: Yes, when the customer contract calls for it. Nadcap AC7114 attaches to the process, not the product stage. A shop running fluorescent penetrant on its own machined details for a Nadcap subscriber prime is performing an accredited special process and needs the baseline AC7114 accreditation plus the penetrant method supplement. In-house use for internal screening only is the sole exception.

facets.q: Can an outsourced Level III sign the written practice, or does NAS 410 require an employee?
facets.a: NAS 410 permits an outside Level 3 engaged under contract, and the aerospace industry has used the arrangement for decades. What the standard does not permit is ambiguity: the written practice must name the Responsible Level 3, define the scope of that person's authority by method, and show that the employer retains responsibility for the program. Auditors check the contract, not just the signature.

facets.q: How long before an AC7114 audit should a Wichita supplier bring in a Level III?
facets.a: Six months for a first accreditation, because the personnel files are the long pole. NAS 410 Revision 5 requires the specific examination after 75% of the experience hours and the practical after 100%, so technicians short on documented hours cannot be examined into compliance on a deadline. The Performance Review Institute also requires a completed self-audit thirty days before the visit.

facets.q: My shop does new-build work for Textron Aviation and repair work under Part 145. Do I need two programs?
facets.a: Two documents, one Level III. The manufacturing side runs on a NAS 410 written practice audited under AC7114. The repair station side runs on an NDI program described inside the repair station manual and accepted by the FAA under 14 CFR 145.155 and AC 65-31B. The same person can author and sign both, and the technician certifications can be common, but the governing documents stay separate.

facets.q: What does an AC7114 auditor open first in a small Wichita shop?
facets.a: The written practice, then the personnel file of whoever last signed a report. The auditor traces one part backwards: report signature to certification record, certification record to examination package, examination package to the written practice clause that authorised it, and the procedure used back to the customer's process specification. A break anywhere in that chain is the finding.

facets.q: We inspect composite bonded structure. Which method qualification does the Level III need?
facets.a: Ultrasonic, at minimum, and the procedure has to name the specific reference standard. Wichita's composite density — fuselage sections, Kaman's off-aircraft repair work, Bell rotorcraft structure — means through-transmission and pulse-echo scanning against engineered-disbond standards. A Level III qualified only in penetrant and magnetic particle cannot approve those procedures, and an auditor will catch the mismatch in the first hour.

sections.heading: What Wichita's supply base actually sends through a penetrant line
paragraphs: The Wichita plant Boeing acquired from Spirit AeroSystems in 2025 builds fuselage sections for the 737 and 787 plus flight deck sections for most Boeing airliners — roughly seventy percent of the 737's structure originates there. Textron Aviation builds Cessna and Beechcraft airframes across the city and keeps its headquarters at Dwight D. Eisenhower National Airport alongside more than sixty other aviation businesses. Airbus took over the A220 pylon line in Wichita during the same transaction, and Bell's Wichita Assembly Center builds V-280 fuselages for the Army's Future Long Range Assault Aircraft.

None of that hardware reaches final assembly without inspection, and most of the inspection happens upstream. Fluorescent penetrant runs on machined aluminium and titanium details. Magnetic particle runs on steel fittings, gear components and forgings. Ultrasonic runs on plate stock, bonded composite structure and thin machined pockets. Radiography runs on castings and fusion welds. Those processes sit inside the roughly 350 supplier firms in the greater Wichita region rather than inside the primes, which is exactly why the audit burden lands on companies with twenty to a hundred and fifty employees.

That distribution is the commercial fact behind this page. A shop operating a penetrant line, a magnetic particle bench or an ultrasonic station is an NDT employer under the National Aerospace Standard NAS 410, whatever its headcount. It owes a written practice, controlled method procedures, qualification examinations and personnel records — the same obligations Textron Aviation carries, discharged by a company with one quality manager, two inspectors and nobody holding a Level III certificate.

sections.heading: The regime: NAS 410 first, AC7114 second, the prime's own list third
paragraphs: NAS 410 Revision 5, issued in September 2020, remains the current revision and is the aerospace industry's personnel qualification standard. It defines Level 1, Level 2, Level 3 and Senior Level 3, requires the employer to maintain a written practice, and requires a named Responsible Level 3 to own the programme. Revision 5 tightened the sequencing that trips up most first-time applicants: the specific examination is administered after a minimum of 75% of the required experience hours, and the practical examination after 100%.

Nadcap AC7114 is the baseline nondestructive testing audit criteria administered by the Performance Review Institute, supported by method-specific supplements covering penetrant, magnetic particle, ultrasonic, radiography and eddy current. There is no route to a method accreditation that skips the AC7114 baseline. The programme also requires the supplier to complete a self-audit against the official checklists at least thirty days before the auditor arrives — a step small shops routinely discover a fortnight out.

The third gate is the one Wichita suppliers underestimate. A prime's own approved-processor listing sits above Nadcap, with its own process specifications and acceptance criteria. Holding the certificate does not put a shop on the list. Our [Nadcap AC7114 audit readiness work](/consulting/nadcap-ac7114-audit-readiness) treats the two as separate deliverables, because a supplier that clears the audit and still cannot ship has bought nothing.

sections.heading: Why the Level III chair sits empty in Wichita specifically
paragraphs: Wichita produces NDT technicians in volume. The National Center for Aviation Training at WSU Tech runs nondestructive testing programmes alongside composites and aviation maintenance. The National Institute for Aviation Research operates six locations across the city with more than a million square feet of laboratory space, and the metro carries roughly eleven thousand engineering-related employees across manufacturers and suppliers. Level I and Level II candidates are available here in a way they simply are not in most American manufacturing regions.

What the metro does not produce in volume is Level IIIs, and the few it produces get absorbed immediately. A sixty-person machine shop on the west side competes for that person against Boeing's Wichita operation, Textron Aviation, Bell and NIAR — organisations that can offer a career ladder, method breadth and a research budget. The shop loses that competition every time, then discovers its next audit has no signatory.

The outsourced arrangement exists because the alternative is a vacancy. Under contract, an ASNT Level III occupies [the Responsible Level 3 role NAS 410 defines](/consulting/nas-410-responsible-level-3), holds the method scope the shop actually needs, and is present for the audit. The shop pays for the function rather than the headcount, and the function is what the auditor is looking for.

sections.heading: The ninety days before an AC7114 audit
paragraphs: The first task is not opening the checklist. It is reading the customer flowdowns — the purchase order clauses, the process specifications and the acceptance criteria each Wichita prime imposes — and building the written practice backwards from them. A written practice assembled from a template will pass a superficial read and fail on the first traceability trace, because the template does not know that one customer calls NAS 410 while another names an internal spec. [Building the written practice from the customer specifications backwards](/consulting/written-practice-development) is the whole job.

Procedures come next, and they have to be method-specific, part-family-specific and approved by a Level III qualified in that method. A generic ultrasonic procedure covering plate, forgings and bonded composite in four pages is a finding waiting to happen. Technique sheets have to name the reference standard, the equipment configuration and the scan plan. [Method procedures written to the customer's process specification](/consulting/ndt-technical-procedure-development) are what survive an auditor's sampling.

Personnel files close the sequence. Every technician needs a training record, an experience log meeting the Revision 5 gates, general, specific and practical examination packages, vision test results and an annual evaluation. The self-audit is then run against the official checklists and answered thirty days before the visit. Shops that start this ninety days out finish it. Shops that start six weeks out reschedule.

sections.heading: Composite bondline inspection is the Wichita-specific technical problem
paragraphs: No other American aerospace metro concentrates composite structure the way Wichita does. Fuselage sections for the 787 are built here. Kaman Composite Structures runs off-aircraft composite repair, inspection and testing in the city. NIAR was designated lead institution for the Center of Excellence in Composites and Advanced Materials by NASA and the FAA. Bell's rotorcraft structure is composite-heavy, and the V-280 fuselage assembly work now landing in Wichita brings that content with it.

That changes what a competent NDT programme looks like. Bonded structure is inspected by through-transmission and pulse-echo ultrasonics, resonance and mechanical impedance methods, and occasionally thermography — against reference standards containing engineered disbonds and porosity levels that match the laminate being inspected. A procedure that names a generic step wedge instead of the correct reference standard is not a procedure an auditor will accept.

The implication for the Level III is method scope. A Level III holding penetrant and magnetic particle only cannot approve ultrasonic procedures for bonded structure, cannot examine the technicians running them, and cannot answer the auditor's questions about reference standard control and calibration intervals. Wichita engagements should be scoped on the methods the shop actually operates, not the methods that were cheapest to certify.

sections.heading: The repair-station layer: Wichita's MRO and modification work
paragraphs: Eisenhower National hosts what is described as the world's largest general aviation MRO facility. Kaman Composite Structures holds an FAA Part 145 repair station certificate at its Wichita location for off-aircraft composite repair, inspection and testing. Embraer runs a business jet service centre at Colonel James Jabara Airport. Bombardier continues to support the Learjet fleet from Wichita after the final Learjet 75 was delivered on 28 March 2022. Around all of them sits a subcontract layer of paint, machining, plating and inspection shops.

This layer answers to a different authority. 14 CFR 145.155 requires a certificated repair station to ensure inspection personnel are thoroughly familiar with the applicable regulations and inspection methods and proficient with the equipment involved. The NDI programme itself lives in the repair station manual, and FAA AC 65-31B sets out the recommended criteria for training, qualifying and certifying nondestructive inspection personnel. [The Part 145 side of aviation NDT](/consulting/aviation-ndt-consulting) is governed by an FAA acceptance, not a Nadcap certificate.

A Wichita firm that does both — and many do — needs both documents. The technician certifications can be common where scope and method match, but a NAS 410 written practice pasted into a repair station manual will be rejected, and an FAA-accepted NDI programme submitted at an AC7114 audit clears nothing. Two governing documents, one Level III, one set of people.

sections.heading: New owners, new flowdowns: what changed in Wichita in 2025
paragraphs: Boeing completed its acquisition of Spirit AeroSystems in 2025, and Airbus simultaneously took ownership of the Wichita A220 pylon production. One site that had operated under a single supplier quality system now feeds two different customers with two different sets of process specifications and two different auditor populations. Suppliers who had one flowdown to satisfy now reconcile two, and the reconciliation shows up first in NDT because NDT is where the acceptance criteria differ most.

Bell's Wichita Assembly Center adds a third pattern. A new production programme means a new supplier approval cycle, and shops that hold current accreditation get invited into it while shops that let it lapse re-audit from scratch. Bell's June 2026 reduction of 285 positions across Fort Worth, Amarillo and Wichita is a reminder of how fast this base resets — the suppliers who stay qualified are the ones positioned for the next award rather than the last one.

The same logic runs down I-35 to the Texas fighter and rotorcraft base, where the mix of build-side and repair-side audit regimes is even sharper. Our [Fort Worth and DFW aerospace NDT page](/consulting/aerospace-ndt-consulting-fort-worth) covers that market. Firms with plants in both metros usually run one written practice with two site annexes rather than two independent programmes.

sections.heading: What the outsourced Level III will not do for a Wichita shop
paragraphs: The signature does not create compliance. An outside Level III cannot certify a technician he has not examined, cannot approve a procedure for a method he is not qualified in, and cannot make experience hours appear that were never logged. NAS 410 leaves responsibility for the programme with the employer regardless of who holds the pen — a point auditors make explicitly when they ask who the Responsible Level 3 reports to inside the company.

Nor does the arrangement replace the quality manager. Someone on site controls the documents, maintains the calibration records, keeps the reference standards under control and runs the day-to-day process. The Level III sets the technical requirements, approves the technical documents, examines the people and attends the audit. Shops that expect the outside Level III to also run the quality system are buying the wrong service.

What Atlantis provides is the qualified signatory, the documents that signatory is willing to sign, the examination programme behind the certifications, and attendance when the auditor arrives. It is affordable, accessible and fully customisable to the methods and customers a given Wichita shop actually has. [Tell us your customers and audit date](/contact) and we will scope it — quote on request.

faq.q: Is an ASNT NDT Level III certificate the same thing as being certified to work at my company?
faq.a: No, and the distinction is the whole reason outsourced Level IIIs exist. The ASNT certificate attests that an individual passed third-party basic and method examinations. Employer certification is separate: under SNT-TC-1A and NAS 410 the employer certifies its own personnel against its own written practice, and needs a qualified Level III to write that practice and administer the examinations. The certificate qualifies the person to hold the role. The written practice is what actually certifies your technicians.

faq.q: Our Wichita shop has never been audited. What is the realistic sequence to a first Nadcap accreditation?
faq.a: Scope the methods and customers, then build the written practice from the customer flowdowns. Write and approve method procedures and technique sheets. Reconstruct or complete technician experience logs, then administer general, specific and practical examinations in the order NAS 410 Revision 5 requires. Complete the self-audit against the official checklists at least thirty days before the visit and close the findings you generate yourself. Then host the audit with the Level III present.

faq.q: We use a subcontract NDT house instead of running our own line. Do we still need a Level III?
faq.a: Not for the processes you subcontract, provided the subcontractor holds the relevant accreditation and your purchase orders flow the correct specification down to them. You do need a documented process for approving and monitoring that supplier, and someone competent to review the reports they return. Firms that run any in-house inspection at all — including in-process visual to a written standard — carry the full employer obligation for that scope.

faq.q: Can one Level III cover multiple Wichita companies at the same time?
faq.a: Yes, and it is common practice across the metro. What matters is that each employer's written practice names the individual, defines the method scope, and is supported by a contract showing the availability and authority the role requires. Auditors probe whether the Level III has enough presence to discharge the duties described. A named signatory who has never been on site cannot answer that question, so the engagement has to include real time in the building.

faq.q: Does Atlantis provide the technician training as well as the Level III function?
faq.a: Yes. Level I and Level II training delivered to your own written practice keeps the classroom content, the specific examination and the procedures aligned, which is what an auditor traces. Our [corporate NDT training programmes](/corporate-ndt-training) are built around the methods and part families a given shop actually inspects rather than a generic syllabus. Atlantis does not provide API 510, 570 or 653 training — that is outside our scope.

title: Fort Worth Aerospace NDT: Nadcap and Part 145 Under One Level III
description: Lockheed's F-35 line, Bell's rotorcraft programs and a dense Part 145 population put two NDT audit regimes on DFW firms. One outsourced Level III covers both.
h1: Aerospace and Aviation NDT Consulting for Fort Worth and DFW
answer: Fort Worth runs two inspection economies at once. Suppliers feeding the F-35 line at Air Force Plant 4 and Bell's rotorcraft programs need Nadcap AC7114 and prime process approval. Repair stations across Alliance, Meacham and DFW need an NDI program accepted under 14 CFR 145.155. One contracted Level III can hold both documents.
expansion: Dallas–Fort Worth holds the largest concentration of tactical aircraft manufacturing in the country. Lockheed Martin Aeronautics runs F-35 final assembly at Air Force Plant 4, a government-owned plant that grew past 6.5 million square feet and employs roughly 17,000 people, sitting beside NAS Fort Worth Joint Reserve Base on the former Carswell field. Bell Textron is headquartered in the metro and is standing up a 447,000-square-foot FLRAA component factory targeting low-rate initial production readiness in 2028. Elbit Systems of America keeps its US headquarters in Fort Worth, Triumph Fabrications operates on East Lancaster Avenue, and Lockheed Martin Missiles and Fire Control and Airbus Helicopters both sit in Grand Prairie. Underneath them are hundreds of machining, forming, processing and repair firms. Two separate qualification regimes govern their NDT: Nadcap AC7114 with NAS 410 personnel files on the build side, and an FAA-accepted NDI programme under Part 145 on the repair side.
source: Verified against: 14 CFR Part 145, specifically 145.155 (Inspection personnel requirements); FAA AC 65-31B on training, qualification and certification of nondestructive inspection personnel; NAS 410 Revision 5 (September 2020) and its 75%/100% experience gates; Nadcap AC7114 baseline audit criteria and the Performance Review Institute's 30-day self-audit rule; public record on Air Force Plant 4 (government-owned, Lockheed Martin Aeronautics operated, F-35 final assembly, approximately 17,000 employees, adjacent to NAS Fort Worth JRB); Bell Textron's announcement of a 447,000 sq ft FLRAA component facility in the Fort Worth region with LRIP readiness targeted for 2028, and its June 2026 reduction of 285 positions across Fort Worth, Amarillo and Wichita; Elbit Systems of America corporate headquarters listing; Triumph Fabrications Fort Worth location; American Airlines maintenance network including the Tulsa base and Fort Worth operations; ASTM E1417 and E1444 as the penetrant and magnetic particle standards commonly cited on defence purchase orders.

table.note: A DFW firm doing both new-build and repair work needs two personnel-qualification documents, not one. The repair station manual has to describe its NDI programme in its own right, and an FAA-accepted programme does not clear AC7114. The technician certifications underneath them can be shared where method and scope match.

facets.q: Is Nadcap accreditation enough to get onto a prime's approved processor list in Fort Worth?
facets.a: No. Nadcap accreditation demonstrates that your special process meets industry baseline criteria. A prime's approved processor listing is a separate commercial and technical approval against that prime's own process specifications, acceptance criteria and often a first-article demonstration. Most DFW suppliers need both, held simultaneously. Losing one does not automatically revoke the other, and holding the certificate alone does not authorise shipment.

facets.q: What does 14 CFR 145.155 actually require of NDI personnel at a DFW repair station?
facets.a: It requires the certificated repair station to ensure that persons performing inspections are thoroughly familiar with the applicable regulations and with the inspection methods, techniques, practices, aids, equipment and tools used, proficient with that equipment, and able to understand, read and write English. The detail of how you qualify them lives in the repair station manual, and AC 65-31B sets out the criteria the FAA recommends.

facets.q: Our Level III just left for Lockheed or Bell. What breaks first?
facets.a: Procedure approvals. Any procedure revision, new technique sheet or new part family stops immediately because nobody can sign. Next, technician certifications lapse at their renewal dates with no one authorised to examine or evaluate. Third, your written practice names a person who no longer works there, which is a finding on sight. Customer approvals follow within a quarter.

facets.q: Do rotorcraft dynamic components need a different NDT programme than airframe details?
facets.a: They need different procedures and different Level III method scope, inside the same written practice. Dynamic components — gears, shafts, hubs and drive train parts — drive fluorescent penetrant at higher sensitivity levels, wet fluorescent magnetic particle on steel, and eddy current on rotating surfaces, with acceptance criteria set by the airworthiness consequence of a missed indication rather than by the manufacturing process.

facets.q: Can one Level III cover a Fort Worth manufacturing plant and a separate Part 145 station?
facets.a: Yes, and it is the efficient arrangement for firms that run both. The person is named as Responsible Level 3 in the manufacturing written practice and as the technical authority for the NDI programme in the repair station manual. The two documents stay separate because two different authorities accept them, but one signatory, one examination programme and one set of technician records supports both.

facets.q: Which methods do DFW fighter and rotorcraft suppliers most often need procedures for?
facets.a: Fluorescent penetrant dominates, because titanium and aluminium machined details are the volume work at Air Force Plant 4's supply base. Magnetic particle follows for high-strength steel fittings and landing gear components. Ultrasonic covers plate, forgings and bonded structure. Eddy current appears on rotorcraft dynamic components and fastener holes. Radiography sits mainly with the casting and weld suppliers.

sections.heading: The DFW aerospace base, facility by facility
paragraphs: Air Force Plant 4 is the anchor. Government-owned and operated by Lockheed Martin Aeronautics at 1 Lockheed Boulevard, it has built B-24s, B-36s, B-58s, F-111s and F-16s, and now runs F-35 Lightning II final assembly with roughly 17,000 employees on a site that expanded past 6.5 million square feet. NAS Fort Worth Joint Reserve Base, the former Carswell Air Force Base, sits immediately adjacent and hosts Air Force Reserve, Navy, Marine Corps and Air National Guard flying units with their own inspection requirements.

Bell Textron is headquartered in the metro, with rotorcraft engineering, composites and manufacturing across Fort Worth and Hurst. Bell selected a 447,000-square-foot facility in the Fort Worth region for Future Long Range Assault Aircraft component manufacturing, working toward low-rate initial production readiness in 2028, with final airframe assembly in Amarillo and fuselage assembly in Wichita. Elbit Systems of America runs its US headquarters in Fort Worth, and Triumph Fabrications operates a parts manufacturing site on East Lancaster Avenue.

East of the city the mix changes. Lockheed Martin Missiles and Fire Control is in Grand Prairie, as is Airbus Helicopters' North American operation. American Airlines is headquartered in Fort Worth and runs its largest maintenance base in Tulsa, 250 miles up the turnpike and the largest airline-owned MRO in the world, with maintenance and engine test activity in the Alliance corridor where Rolls-Royce established engine test operations at a former American facility.

sections.heading: Two audit regimes in one metro, and the firms caught between them
paragraphs: The manufacturing half of DFW runs on Nadcap. A shop supplying machined details, formed parts, castings, weldments or processed hardware into Air Force Plant 4 or Bell answers to AC7114 baseline audit criteria plus method supplements, backed by NAS 410 personnel qualification and a written practice naming a Responsible Level 3. The Performance Review Institute requires a self-audit against the official checklists thirty days before the auditor arrives, and the personnel files are what the auditor samples first.

The maintenance half runs on FAA acceptance. Repair stations across Alliance, Meacham International and DFW International carry inspection personnel obligations under 14 CFR 145.155 and describe their NDI programme inside the repair station manual, with AC 65-31B setting out the recommended training, qualification and certification criteria. [Aviation NDT consulting for Part 145 organisations](/consulting/aviation-ndt-consulting) is a different deliverable from a Nadcap readiness engagement, even when the same technicians do the work.

A meaningful number of DFW firms sit in both. A component shop that manufactures new parts and also holds a repair station certificate for overhaul of the same part family needs a written practice for the first and an NDI programme for the second. Trying to satisfy both with one document produces a finding from whichever auditor reads it second. One Level III, two governing documents, one examination programme underneath.

sections.heading: What the F-35 supply chain demands of an inspection programme
paragraphs: Fifth-generation fighter structure is titanium and high-strength steel in quantities that change the inspection profile. Titanium machined details drive fluorescent penetrant at controlled sensitivity levels, with etch requirements before inspection that are themselves specification-controlled. High-strength steel drives wet fluorescent magnetic particle with demagnetisation and field-strength verification. Machined pockets and thin webs drive ultrasonic thickness and flaw detection. Every one of those is a Nadcap special process with a method supplement behind it.

The specification layer is where DFW suppliers lose time. Lockheed Martin flows its own process specifications and acceptance criteria down alongside the Nadcap requirement, and those criteria differ from what a supplier may already run for a commercial customer. Writing one generic penetrant procedure and submitting it to every buyer is the single most common cause of a rejected first article in this supply base. [Procedures written to the customer's process specification](/consulting/nadcap-ac7114-audit-readiness) are the deliverable, not procedures written to the standard in general.

The Level III's job here is translation. Someone has to read the purchase order, identify which specification and revision governs, write the procedure to it, prove the technique on representative hardware, qualify the technicians against that procedure, and hold the records so an auditor can trace a finished part back to the person who inspected it and the document that authorised them.

sections.heading: Rotorcraft: Bell's expansion and dynamic-component inspection
paragraphs: Rotorcraft NDT is not scaled-down fixed-wing NDT. Dynamic components — main rotor hubs, gearbox internals, drive shafts, swashplate parts — carry loads that make a missed indication an airworthiness event rather than a scrap decision. That drives higher penetrant sensitivity levels, wet fluorescent magnetic particle rather than dry powder, eddy current on rotating surfaces and fastener holes, and acceptance criteria written around fatigue-critical locations rather than general workmanship.

Bell's Fort Worth component factory, Amarillo final assembly and Wichita fuselage work together represent a new production programme rather than an extension of an old one, which means a supplier approval cycle rather than a rollover. Bell's June 2026 reduction of 285 positions across those three sites is a reminder that the supply base resets faster than most suppliers plan for. Firms holding current accreditation get invited into the next round. Firms whose certificate lapsed re-audit from zero.

The practical consequence for a Fort Worth shop chasing rotorcraft work is method scope. If the Level III named in your written practice holds penetrant and magnetic particle but not eddy current, you cannot approve eddy current procedures, cannot examine technicians in it, and cannot bid the dynamic-component work that pays for the programme. [Scope the Level III engagement to the methods you actually operate](/consulting/outside-ndt-level-3-can-and-cannot-do) before the contract is signed.

sections.heading: Part 145 repair stations: what the FAA inspector actually opens
paragraphs: A repair station audit follows a different logic from a Nadcap audit. The inspector starts from the certificate and operations specifications, works into the repair station manual and quality control manual, and asks whether the organisation is doing what those documents say. NDI is one section of that, and the section has to describe how personnel are trained, qualified, certified and re-evaluated, and against which standard — AC 65-31B recognises that several qualification standards can serve, provided the chosen one is written into the accepted manual.

The failure mode is inheritance. A repair station that grew out of a manufacturing operation frequently carries a NAS 410 written practice into its manual by reference, without reconciling it against 145.155 or against the OEM maintenance manual requirements that actually govern the inspections being performed. The inspector reads the manual, then reads a work card, then finds the technique the technician used is not in either document.

An outsourced Level III writing for a DFW repair station works from the maintenance data outward: the OEM manual revision in force, the technique it specifies, the equipment and reference standards it calls for, then the qualification programme that certifies the person to run it. [Examination and qualification oversight](/consulting/ndt-level-3-exam-oversight) is the part that has to be genuinely independent, because the inspector will ask who administered the practical and what they were qualified to judge.

sections.heading: Grand Prairie, missiles and the ASTM-cited purchase order
paragraphs: Defence work east of Fort Worth changes the paperwork. Missile and munition contracts frequently cite ASTM E1417 for liquid penetrant and ASTM E1444 for magnetic particle directly on the purchase order, rather than pointing to a prime's internal process specification. Suppliers who have only ever worked to a prime spec read this as a simplification. It is not — the ASTM standards carry their own process control, system performance check and documentation requirements, and they are revision-sensitive.

AS9100 sits above it, and its treatment of special processes matters here. NDT performed as a special process requires validation that the process achieves planned results, with personnel qualification as part of that validation. Suppliers who log NDT as an inspection activity rather than a validated special process produce an audit trail their customer's quality engineer cannot accept, regardless of how good the inspection itself was.

Government source inspection adds a second reviewer. DCMA can review the quality system on site, and when it does, the personnel certification records have to reconcile with the written practice on that day — not after a weekend of file reconstruction. The [NAS 410 certification requirements page](/nas-410-certification-requirements) sets out what a complete personnel file contains and in what order the evidence has to sit.

sections.heading: Losing a Level III in a market that outbids you
paragraphs: DFW has one of the strongest aerospace labour markets in the country and a corresponding retention problem for small firms. Lockheed Martin, Bell, Elbit, American Airlines and the engine overhaul operations in the Alliance corridor all recruit experienced Level IIIs, and they can offer method breadth, structured progression and stability that a forty-person processing shop cannot match. The shop trains someone to Level III, then loses them within two years.

The damage is not gradual. Procedure approvals stop the day the person leaves, because nobody else can sign. Technician certifications begin lapsing at their next renewal dates with no authorised examiner. The written practice names someone who no longer works there, which is a visible finding to any auditor who opens it. Customer approvals that depend on a named technical authority come under review within a quarter.

Contracting the function converts a retention risk into a service agreement. The named Responsible Level 3 does not resign to a competitor, the method scope is fixed by contract rather than by whoever happened to be available, and continuity across an audit cycle stops depending on one individual's career decisions. Wichita firms face an identical squeeze against Boeing, Textron Aviation and NIAR, covered on our [Wichita aerospace NDT page](/consulting/aerospace-ndt-consulting-wichita).

sections.heading: How the engagement runs, and where its authority stops
paragraphs: An Atlantis engagement in DFW starts with the customer documents rather than the audit checklist: purchase order clauses, process specifications and revisions, OEM maintenance data where a repair station is involved, and the methods and part families actually in the building. From that we build or rebuild the written practice, write and approve method procedures and technique sheets, construct the examination programme, complete the personnel files, run the self-audit and attend the audit itself.

The limits are real and worth stating before the contract. An outside Level III cannot certify technicians he has not examined, cannot approve procedures in methods he is not qualified in, and cannot manufacture experience hours that were never recorded. The employer keeps responsibility for the programme under NAS 410 and keeps the accountable manager's obligations under Part 145. Someone on site still controls documents, calibration and reference standards day to day.

What we supply is the qualified signatory, the technical documents that signatory will stand behind, the examination programme that makes your certifications defensible, and presence in the room when the auditor arrives. Affordable, accessible and fully customisable to the specific mix of Nadcap and Part 145 obligations a given DFW firm carries. [Send us your customer list and audit date](/contact) — quote on request.

faq.q: We supply into Air Force Plant 4 but only do machining, no in-house processing. Does any of this apply?
faq.a: Only partly. If every special process is subcontracted to accredited houses and your purchase orders flow the correct specification and revision down to them, you do not carry the employer obligation for those processes. You do need a documented supplier approval and monitoring process, and someone competent to review the reports coming back. The moment you bring any inspection in-house — including in-process visual to a written acceptance standard — the full obligation attaches.

faq.q: How does a DFW repair station get its NDI programme accepted by the FAA?
faq.a: By writing it into the repair station manual and having the manual accepted through the local Flight Standards District Office. The section has to identify the qualification standard adopted, describe training, examination, certification and re-evaluation, name the technical authority, and align with the maintenance data actually being used. AC 65-31B sets out the criteria the FAA recommends. Acceptance is of the manual, not of a separate certificate.

faq.q: Our contract cites ASTM E1417 rather than a Lockheed or Bell process spec. Does that simplify things?
faq.a: It changes them rather than simplifying them. ASTM E1417 carries its own process control, system performance check, lighting verification and documentation requirements, and those requirements are revision-specific. A procedure written to one revision and audited against another is a finding. The written practice and the procedures both have to name the revision the purchase order cites, and change control has to catch it when the customer moves to a newer one.

faq.q: Can Atlantis attend the Nadcap audit or the FAA visit with us?
faq.a: Yes. Attendance is part of the engagement, because the questions an auditor asks about examination administration, procedure approval authority and method scope are questions only the Level III can answer. A written practice signed by someone who has never appeared on site invites exactly the line of questioning that produces findings. We would rather be in the room than write a response letter afterwards.

faq.q: We have plants in both Fort Worth and Wichita. Do we need two written practices?
faq.a: One written practice with site-specific annexes is usually the cleaner structure, provided the Responsible Level 3 scope covers both sites and the annexes capture the differences in equipment, reference standards and customer specifications. Two fully independent programmes double the maintenance burden and create drift between them. Where the two sites hold different accreditations or serve different customers, the annex approach keeps the common material common and the differences visible.

title: Huntsville NDT Level III: NASA-STD-5009, Nadcap and Missile Work
description: Redstone, NASA Marshall, L3Harris rocket motors and ULA Decatur each impose a different NDT authority. What an outsourced ASNT Level III has to produce for each.
h1: Aerospace NDT Consulting in Huntsville: Rocket City Audit Clearance
answer: Huntsville suppliers answer to three different authorities. NASA Marshall imposes NASA-STD-5009 flaw-detection capability on fracture-critical hardware, Army missile contracts cite ASTM E1417 and E1444 by purchase order, and L3Harris, Blue Origin and ULA flow down Nadcap AC7114. None of those certify people. A NAS 410 written practice signed by a qualified Level III does, and Atlantis supplies one.
expansion: Huntsville's inspection demand comes from hardware that flies once. Redstone Arsenal covers roughly 38,000 acres, employs more than 35,000 people and hosts over 60 agencies including Army Materiel Command, Aviation and Missile Command, the Program Executive Offices for Aviation and for Missiles and Space, and Redstone Test Center. NASA's Marshall Space Flight Center sits inside the same fence line. L3Harris, which absorbed Aerojet Rocketdyne, runs two advanced manufacturing facilities in the city totalling more than half a million square feet, producing solid rocket motor cases, nozzles, exit cones and aft closures for Standard Missile, GMLRS and Javelin. Blue Origin builds BE-4 engines here for New Glenn and for ULA's Vulcan, and United Launch Alliance's 1.5-million-square-foot Decatur plant forty minutes west builds Atlas V and Vulcan structures. The tier-two shops feeding all of them need a documented NDT programme, and most do not employ a Level III.
source: Verified against: NASA-STD-5009, Nondestructive Evaluation Requirements for Fracture-Critical Metallic Components, and NASA-STD-5019 fracture control requirements; NAS 410 Revision 5 (September 2020); Nadcap AC7114 baseline audit criteria and the Performance Review Institute self-audit requirement; ASTM E1417 (liquid penetrant) and ASTM E1444 (magnetic particle) as the standards commonly cited on Army and defence purchase orders; North Alabama Industrial Development Association industry profile for Redstone Arsenal acreage, employment, agency count and annual federal budget, and for the United Launch Alliance Decatur facility size and product lines; L3Harris press releases on the Huntsville Advanced Manufacturing Facility North (136,000 sq ft, opened 2019) and South (379,000 sq ft, over $20 million in renovation, 40 jobs created with more than 100 projected) and the programmes those facilities support; public reporting on Blue Origin's Huntsville rocket engine factory producing BE-4 engines; Cummings Research Park company and employment figures.
